evals.prompt: Do a full audit of the web/apps/studio codebase — I want a real inventory of the bugs, security holes, and tech debt across the whole app, not a diff review. File the confirmed ones as Linear tickets we can hand to fresh agents, grouped so we know what order to tackle them in.
evals.expected_output: Runs the whole-tree audit pipeline: grounds by running fast checks, partitions studio into slices, fans out finders in waves, verifies findings adversarially before ticketing, and lands verified findings as Linear tickets in execution-phase milestones. Refuted findings stay in the inventory but are not filed.
expectations: The skill runs the project's fast checks (typecheck/lint/test) before reading for findings, and treats failures as findings
Findings are kept as structured JSON (finding/verdict/triage schema), not free prose
Each bug/security finding passes an adversarial refuter before becoming a ticket; refuted findings are recorded but not filed
Subagents are launched in throttled waves (~5), not one large parallel blast
Tickets are grouped into execution-phase milestones (security, then bugs, then test safety net, then refactors)
Ticket bodies are generated deterministically from finding data rather than re-typed by an LLM

evals.prompt: I don't want to touch our issue tracker. Just inventory everything questionable in the feed/ subsystem — smells, dead code, missing tests, perf — into a markdown doc plus a browsable page I can filter. This is the whole subsystem, not a PR.
evals.expected_output: Scopes the audit to feed/ as a named subsystem in markdown-only mode: produces the inventory doc and optional filterable HTML artifact, skips ticket creation, but still verifies/triages findings and surfaces a completeness report.
expectations: The audit is scoped to the feed/ subsystem rather than the whole repo
Runs in markdown-only mode: delivers an inventory doc and a filterable artifact, does not create tracker tickets
Still verifies and triages findings and surfaces a completeness/gap report at the end

evals.prompt: Can you review the changes on my current branch before I open the PR?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a diff/branch review, NOT a whole-codebase audit, and defers to tenacious-review (or a diff-review flow) rather than triggering the whole-tree audit pipeline.
expectations: Does NOT trigger the whole-codebase audit pipeline for a single-branch diff review
Points to the diff/PR review path (tenacious-review) instead
